pages.api:
# API reference

> The stream, the report, the store vector, the export endpoints and the settings.

## Stream read: `audio.pcm/<source>`

Schema `pcm.s16le.v1`, class `stream`. Each record is 640 bytes: 320 mono samples of signed 16-bit little-endian PCM at 16 kHz (20 ms). A record of any other length is skipped. `seq` counts from 1 and a gap is a drop.

## Reading `telemetry/<name>`

`telemetry.v1`: `chunks.played`, `chunks.dropped`, `write.errors`, `latency` (ms), `level.rms` (dBFS), `stream.seq`, `bus.connected`.

## stdout report (one per interval)

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `ok`, `no_source`, `simulate`, `replay` |
| `provenance` | string | `MEASURED`, `SYNTHETIC` or `REPLAY` |
| `sink`, `stream` | string | `alsa:<device>` or `null`; `audio.pcm/<source>` |
| `chunks_played`, `chunks_per_s` | numbers | 50 per second when a writer sends real time |
| `dropped_chunks`, `write_errors` | numbers | |
| `latency_ms` | number/null | mean time from the writer's write to this cog's hand-off to ALSA |
| `rms_dbfs`, `peak_dbfs` | number/null | level of what was played |
| `idle` | bool | healthy but nothing arrived in the window |
| `bus` | object | `connected`, `stream_open`, `last_seq`, `error` |
| `error` | string | only with `no_source` |

## Store vector (id 30)

Eight floats; a source that is absent is **-1**.

| Slot | Name | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `rms_dbfs` | dBFS |
| 1 | `peak_dbfs` | dBFS |
| 2 | `chunks_per_s` | per second |
| 3 | `dropped` | chunks |
| 4 | `write_errors` | count |
| 5 | `bus_connected` | 0 or 1 |
| 6 | `latency_ms` | ms, -1 when nothing was played |
| 7 | `active` | 1 if anything was played |

## Export (`http://127.0.0.1:8064`, continuous mode)

`/status` latest report, `/raw` the latest report's raw view, `/history` the last 60 reports, `/guide` this guide, `/healthz`.

## Settings

`--interval`, `--window`, `--source`, `--name`, `--card-name`, `--device`, `--api-bind`, `--replay`, `--simulate`.
pages.device:
# The device

> Which playback card is opened, and how to choose between two.

The host hands the owner the playback nodes it declared (`/dev/snd/pcmC<card>D<device>p`) in the environment variable `WEFTOS_DEVICES`. The cog turns the one it picks into `plughw:<card>,<device>`.

## Choosing between cards

A Ventuno Q has the board codec (card 0, several devices) and, with a USB camera or sound card attached, a USB card. With no setting the cog takes the lowest card and device. To choose another, set **Card name** to part of its name as `/proc/asound/cards` shows it (matched without regard to case).

## By hand

`--device plughw:0,1` opens a device you name, whether or not the host handed it. Use it for a bench run from a shell.

## Ownership

Only one cog owns a playback node. Placing a second cog that declares the same node is refused. So is placing a cog whose arguments name a `/dev/snd/...` path this cog owns.
pages.setup:
# Set up

> Run it from a shell, then place it on the node.

## From a shell

```
cog-audio-out --once --window 3 --replay phrase.wav --device plughw:0,1   # plays the file, prints a report
cog-audio-out --device plughw:0,1                                          # plays audio.pcm/tts0 from the broker
```

With `WEFTOS_COGBUS` and `WEFTOS_COGBUS_TOKEN` set (the host sets them for a placed cog) the cog subscribes to `audio.pcm/<source>` and plays every chunk. The writer is another cog that declares `[[outputs]] topic = "audio.pcm"`, class `stream`, schema `pcm.s16le.v1`, and opens the stream with source id `<source>`.

## Placed on a node

Place `audio-out` through the controller like any cog. Its `cog.toml` declares the device (`[[devices]] path = "/dev/snd/pcmC*D*p"`), the input and the telemetry output. The cog that writes the stream must be in the same project.

## Needs

- `aplay` (alsa-utils) on the board.
- Write access to the playback node for the user the cog runs as (the `audio` group on a stock image).
pages.start:
# Start here

> Make the board's speaker available to every other cog, without any of them opening it.

`audio-out` is the one owner of the playback device. It plays the cogbus stream `audio.pcm/<source>` (default source `tts0`): 16 kHz mono signed 16-bit little-endian PCM in 20 ms chunks (640 bytes). A speech-synthesis cog writes that stream; this cog plays it.

## The short path

1. **See which outputs the board has.** `aplay -l`. → see **The device**
2. **Play a test tone.** `cog-audio-out --once --window 2 --replay tone.wav --device plughw:0,1`. → see **Set up**
3. **Place the cog and a writer.** The host hands this cog the playback node and nothing else. → see **Set up**
4. **Read `dropped_chunks` and `latency_ms`.** Drops mean the writer outran the speaker or the cog fell behind.

You can test with no speaker: `--once --simulate` plays a tone into a null sink, marked `SYNTHETIC`.

## How the signal flows

```diagram
flow
```

## Honest limits

- The stream is a ring in shared memory. A reader that falls a ring behind loses chunks (the `seq` jumps); the cog counts them as `dropped_chunks` and plays on.
- Playback starts when the first chunk arrives. There is no jitter buffer beyond ALSA's own, so a writer that sends in bursts will be heard stutter.
- One writer per stream: the broker allows one writer for `audio.pcm/<source>`. Two writers that should both be heard need two sources and two audio-out instances, which the device ledger refuses (one owner per device). Mixing is not done here.
- On a node where every cog runs under one user id, the node refuses a second claim on the speaker but cannot stop a cog from opening the device behind its back. The listing says `device_isolation: advisory`.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> What each failure looks like and what to do.

## `no_source`

The report's `error` says why.

| `error` starts with | Meaning | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| `no playback node in WEFTOS_DEVICES` | the host handed no playback node | place the cog through the controller, or pass `--device` |
| `no handed playback card matches` | the card name matches none of the handed cards | check `/proc/asound/cards` and the **Card name** setting |
| `aplay: ...` | `aplay` is missing | install alsa-utils |
| `no broker: WEFTOS_COGBUS is not set` | run from a shell without a broker | use `--replay` or `--simulate`, or place the cog |

## Silence but chunks are played

`chunks_played` grows and `rms_dbfs` is above -60 but nothing is heard: the output is muted or routed elsewhere. Check `amixer -c 0 contents` and unmute the playback control.

## `idle: true`

The stream has no writer yet, or the writer is quiet. Check that the cog that writes `audio.pcm/<source>` is running and uses the same source id.

## `dropped_chunks` grows

The cog was starved for a moment (a busy CPU) or the writer sent faster than real time. The cog plays on from the oldest record still safe to read.

## `bus.error` is set

The broker refused the subscription. `unauthorized` or `unknown_topic` means the cog was placed without its `[[inputs]]`; `cross_project` means the writer is in another project.
